newsitem.title: UK: Commercial Union up on Salomon upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union up on Salomon upgrade.

text.p: Shares in Commercial Union Plc rose in early trade on Friday as analysts at Salomon raised the stock to a "buy" from a "hold" ahead of the start of the insurace sector's interim reporting season next week, dealers said.
CU shares were up 5p at 687-1/2 by 0813 GMT in volume of 325,603 shares, after earlier rising as high as 700p. It reports first half results on August 6.
Salomon analyst Andrew Pitt said he also had "buy" ratings on General Accident Plc (Corrects from Guardian Royal Exchange), which reports next week, and Royal Sun Alliance Plc.
Guardian shares were unchanged at 305p while Royal Sun was down 2-1/2p at 503.

Pitt said his upgrade on CU was based in part on its low market valuation compared with rising asset values. He said it was trading close to its historic low in terms of its price-to-book value, with the valuation of its assets boosted by recent stock and bond market gains.
"It's valuation is just too low," the Salomon analyst said.

Pitt said he was expecting a robust set of results from the sector as a whole, driven by a good performance in companies' international life assurance businesses and strong growth in net asset values.
CU shares received a boost earlier this month from a return of vague bid speculation. Goldman Sachs also raised CU and Guardian Royal to a "trading buy" from "market outperformer."
